issue: Preserve optional metadata for unrelated peer dependencies

Deleting the entire `peerDependenciesMeta` block makes `@opentelemetry/api`, `@opentelemetry/resources`, `@opentelemetry/sdk-metrics`, `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base`, and `@opentelemetry/sdk-logs` required as well. Consumers that do not use those integrations can now receive missing-peer installation failures or warnings; retain `optional: true` for those five peers and remove only the metadata entries for the two trace SDKs.

a.body:
issue: Avoid environment access for omitted parameters

The new guard only avoids `process.env` for truthy configured keys; a normal configuration that omits fields such as `password`, `binary`, or `options` still reaches the environment reads below. In Deno without environment permission, constructing a client with otherwise explicit connection settings therefore still throws; environment access needs a safe fallback or must be skipped when unavailable.

b.body:
issue: Falsy config values do not take precedence

The guard only recognizes truthy configuration values, so an explicit value such as `{ binary: false }` or `{ client_encoding: '' }` still falls through to environment lookup and can be replaced by `PGBINARY` or `PGCLIENT_ENCODING`. Check for the property being defined rather than truthiness when applying config-first precedence.

issue: `config[key]` does not preserve falsy configured values

The truthiness check skips valid configured values such as `false`, `0`, and `''`, so an environment variable or default can override them. For example, `{ binary: false }` with `PGBINARY=true` resolves to `true`; check for property presence or `undefined` instead of truthiness.

`if (config[key])` treats configured values such as `''`, `0`, and `false` as absent, so an environment variable or default can override an explicit configuration value. Use an undefined check so configuration precedence applies to every supplied value.

```suggestion
  if (config[key] !== undefined) {
```

issue: Quoted import strings containing `url(` are skipped

For `primary === 'url'`, this guard returns for any parameter containing the text `url(`, including a valid string import such as `@import "foo url(bar).css"`. The previous parser would report that string for conversion to `url(...)`, but the new guard skips it. Restrict the fast path to an actual parsed `url` function, or otherwise avoid matching text inside quoted strings.

b.body:
issue: Skip filter mistakes quoted strings for URL functions

For `@import "url(foo.css)"` with the `url` option, this regex matches the text inside the quoted string and returns before parsing it, so the rule fails to report that the import uses string notation. Restrict the early check to parsed URL-function nodes, or only use a token-aware predicate.

issue: Filter misses percentages preceded by comments

A valid keyframe selector such as `/* comment */ 0%` can be reported or fixed by the previous unconditional walk, but `HAS_PERCENTAGE` requires `0%` or `100%` to start after whitespace or a comma and therefore skips this rule entirely when a comment immediately precedes the percentage. Make the prefilter comment-aware, or retain a selector parse before filtering.

b.body:
issue: Preserve percentage selectors preceded by comments

`HAS_PERCENTAGE` only matches a percentage immediately preceded by the start of the selector, whitespace, or a comma. A valid keyframe selector such as `/* comment */ 0%` is parsed successfully because comments are ignored by `parseKeyframeSelector`, but this walk filter skips it and the required notation warning is lost. Make the filter account for comments or avoid filtering this case.

a.body:
issue: Match multiline attribute operators

`attributeSelectorWithOperator` uses `.*`, which does not match newline characters. A valid selector such as `a[foo\n=bar]` was previously passed to the three attribute-operator rules because the old checks searched independently for `[` and `=`, but it is now filtered out and never validated. Use a newline-safe pattern that preserves the cheap filter, such as `/\[[^]]*=/`.

b.body:
issue: Match operators across multiline attribute selectors

`/\[.*=/` cannot match an `=` separated from `[` by a newline, so valid selectors such as `[data-value\n=\"x\"]` are excluded from `walkRules` and skipped by the attribute operator and attribute quotes rules. The previous `includes('[') && includes('=')` checks accepted these selectors; use a character class that spans newlines, such as `/\[[^\]]*=/`, or filter only on `[` and retain the parser-based check.

issue: Preserve readonly domains in public signatures

The exported transform functions now accept `number[]`, while the existing public declarations accept `readonly number[]` and none of these helpers mutates the input. TypeScript callers passing a readonly tuple or array will therefore fail to compile after the migration, despite being valid under the previous API. Change the domain parameters and internal guard to accept `readonly number[]`.

issue: Respect explicit `coverage.changed: false`

When `test.changed` is enabled and `coverage.changed` is explicitly set to `false`, this branch still assigns `ctx.config.related` to `changedFiles`, so coverage is filtered despite the documented override and the resolved configuration value. Only inherit `related` when coverage filtering was not explicitly disabled, or base this fallback on the resolved coverage option.

issue: Fail when changed coverage cannot resolve Git state

`findChangedFiles` returns `null` when the project is not inside a Git repository, and converting that to `undefined` disables the filter so the run reports coverage for all files even though `coverage.changed` was requested. Propagate the Git-repository error or otherwise fail the run instead of silently producing unfiltered coverage.

issue: Explicit false still inherits test.changed filtering

When `coverage.changed` is explicitly `false` and `test.changed` is enabled, `this.options.changed` is false but `this.ctx.config.changed` is true, so this branch assigns `config.related` and filters coverage anyway. This violates the documented override behavior and can produce incomplete reports; only fall back to `ctx.config.changed` when the coverage option was actually unspecified, and clear `changedFiles` when filtering is disabled.

issue: Explicit false does not disable inherited coverage filtering

When `test.changed` is set and `coverage.changed` is explicitly `false`, the first branch is skipped and this fallback assigns `ctx.config.related` to `changedFiles`. Coverage is therefore still limited to changed files, contradicting the documented and tested override behavior. Only fall back to `ctx.config.related` when `coverage.changed` is unset; an explicit `false` must clear or bypass the filter.

issue: Propagated references violate older draft rules

For `draft-07`, `draft-04`, and `openapi-3.0`, this unconditionally adds the extracted parent `$ref` to the child schema even when the child retains properties such as `description`. The surrounding code explicitly handles these targets by using `allOf` because they cannot combine `$ref` with sibling properties, so a schema such as `z.string().readonly().meta({ id: "x" }).describe("foo")` emits a `$ref` alongside `description` and loses the intended metadata semantics. Apply the same target-specific `allOf` handling here, or avoid propagating the parent `$ref` directly for these targets.

b.body:
issue: Preserve older-target `$ref` compatibility during parent propagation

For `draft-04`, `draft-07`, and `openapi-3.0`, this assigns a `$ref` directly while leaving wrapper properties such as `description` on the same schema object. Those targets do not support meaningful sibling keywords alongside `$ref`, so metadata on cases such as `z.string().readonly().meta({ id: "job" }).describe("...")` is ignored or produces an invalid schema. Apply the same `allOf` handling used above when the target cannot combine `$ref` with sibling properties.

issue: Strict validation is bypassed when normalization is enabled

The `!def.normalize` guard means `z.httpUrl({ normalize: true })` still passes inputs such as `http:example.com` to `new URL()`, which accepts and normalizes them to a valid HTTP URL. Apply the required `://` check for HTTP URLs regardless of the normalization mode.

b.body:
issue: Enforce strict HTTP syntax for normalized URLs

The `!def.normalize` condition lets `httpUrl({ normalize: true })` pass malformed inputs such as `http:example.com` and `http:/example.com` to `new URL()`, which normalizes them into accepted HTTP URLs. Apply the `://` check for HTTP protocol-constrained schemas regardless of the normalization setting.

issue: Strict validation is bypassed when normalization is enabled

issue: Enforce the separator for normalized HTTP URLs

The `!def.normalize` guard bypasses the new validation for `httpUrl({ normalize: true })`, so inputs such as `http:example.com` and `http:/example.com` reach `new URL()` and are normalized and accepted. This leaves a public `httpUrl()` configuration accepting the malformed forms that the strict-validation change is intended to reject; remove the `!def.normalize` condition or otherwise apply the `://` check to all HTTP URL schemas.
